title: Tower requirements loader + join + view

proposed_solution: Load tower_requirements.csv, join against latest snapshot by normalized item name, and add a read-only Tower page

dependencies: Latest snapshot storage; normalized item key; tower_requirements.csv
notes: Tower CSV loader, pure derivation, and read-only Tower page are implemented
release_notes: Added a Tower view that shows requirement status from your latest local snapshot.

title: Canonical item key formalization
user_value: Reduce fragile joins across mastery, tower, and future planning data
proposed_solution: Define a more explicit canonical item identity contract and migration path beyond normalized names
scope_v1: Documented key strategy and minimal compatibility helpers
dependencies: Current normalized item key flow; reference CSV loaders
notes: Do not force ID migration until data sources are ready

title: Tower data validation
user_value: Catch malformed or inconsistent tower rows before they confuse planning views
proposed_solution: Add validation checks for tower CSV schema, duplicate rows, unsupported mastery tiers, and suspicious blanks
scope_v1: Loader-level validation report or tests for known bad shapes
notes: Shipped with exact required-header validation, required-field checks, unsupported-tier rejection, and duplicate tower level/slot detection in the tower loader. Tower CSV already encodes GM/MM correctly and should stay source of truth.
release_notes: Added runtime validation for malformed tower CSV schemas, tiers, and duplicate slots.

title: Unmatched reference data polish
user_value: Make missing reference matches easier to understand and maintain
proposed_solution: Improve messaging, counts, and export/report affordances for unmatched mastery and tower rows
scope_v1: Display polish and small workflow helpers only
notes: Do not make missing matches fatal

title: Reference CSV schema validation
user_value: prevent silent errors in CSV reference files and improve confidence in data integrity
proposed_solution: add runtime validators for app reference CSV schemas and surface clear non-fatal validation failures where appropriate
scope_v1: validate mastery_difficulty.csv and tower_requirements.csv shape and required fields in their loaders
notes: Shipped with exact required-header validation in the mastery difficulty and tower requirements loaders, plus clearer runtime failures for blank required fields and malformed non-blank mastery difficulty values. planning/backlog.csv itself does not need app-style runtime validation unless later tooling requires it.
release_notes: Added runtime schema validation for the local mastery difficulty and tower requirements CSV loaders.

title: Tower accordion / collapse completed levels
user_value: reduce noise from completed tower levels and make the next relevant mastery targets easier to spot
proposed_solution: add collapsible tower sections with an option to collapse or hide fully completed levels
scope_v1: accordion UI for tower levels with completed levels collapsed by default or hideable, while incomplete levels remain expanded
dependencies: Tower page; grouped tower derivation output
notes: Shipped as a level-based accordion with completed levels collapsed by default, incomplete levels expanded, and the first incomplete level highlighted with its next blocking requirement. Prefer level-based collapse before range-based collapse; avoid derivation changes unless lightweight completed-level summaries are needed. Future nice-to-haves: jump to first incomplete level; sticky next relevant level summary; auto-expand only the first incomplete level; sort incomplete levels above completed ones.
release_notes: Collapsed completed Tower levels by default and highlighted the next blocking Tower requirement.

title: Tower range accordion / completed ranges grouping
user_value: make higher-level Tower progress easier to scan once many level groups are complete
proposed_solution: add a range-level accordion keyed by tower_level_range from tower_requirements.csv, with a top-level Completed ranges section that collects fully completed range groups
scope_v1: top-level completed/incomplete range grouping; accordion by tower_level_range; within each range keep the existing level-level accordion behavior; include a concise per-level summary in the level heading such as "Tower Level 287 - 1/2 items remaining"; within each level keep independent requirement rows
dependencies: Tower page; tower_requirements.csv tower_level_range values; existing level accordion behavior
notes: Shipped with range-level accordions keyed directly from tower_requirements.csv tower_level_range values, a top-level Completed ranges section for fully completed range groups, and concise per-level summaries in the level headings. Completed/incomplete top-level grouping is derived from range completion status and does not recompute ad hoc numeric buckets. Keep this item focused on hierarchy and navigation rather than a full table/detail-card redesign.
release_notes: Grouped Tower levels by tower_level_range and moved fully completed ranges into a collapsed Completed ranges section.

title: Tower detail-card / table cleanup
user_value: make the Tower detail area easier to use for planning once hierarchy and navigation are in place
proposed_solution: simplify the default Tower detail view by hiding debug-oriented columns, using compact requirement-tier labels, reconsidering Notes placement, and emphasizing planning-friendly progress cues like percent complete
scope_v1: presentation cleanup for the default Tower detail area: remove or hide debug-oriented columns such as Match; reconsider whether Notes belongs in the default UI; remove the standalone Slot column from the default table if that information is better surfaced in the level summary; keep the requirement column but use compact default labels such as M, GM, and MM instead of long phrases; add a % complete column for each item; optimize the detail area for planning rather than debugging
dependencies: Tower page hierarchy/navigation improvements; existing Tower row data
notes: Shipped as a presentation cleanup only. Underlying row data remains available even where some columns are hidden from the default view. Row independence and correctness are preserved. The requirement column stays in the table because rows may mix M, GM, and MM, but the default presentation is compact and longer wording can move to future expanded/debug views if needed.
release_notes: Simplified the default Tower detail table with compact M/GM/MM labels and planning-focused progress columns.

title: Detect collapsed mastery export sections
user_value: prevent incomplete mastery imports caused by collapsed export sections
proposed_solution: detect missing mastery tiers during import and show warning with override
scope_v1: warn when expected mastery tiers are missing or the parsed row count is suspiciously small, but still allow import anyway
dependencies: Import page validation layer; parsed row tier analysis
notes: Shipped with non-fatal warning and override. False-positive Tier II warning caused by threshold mismatch was fixed so validation now uses parsed tier thresholds consistently.
release_notes: Added an import warning for likely incomplete mastery exports, with an option to continue anyway.

title: Tower filters and summaries
user_value: Help users inspect tower requirements faster
proposed_solution: Add simple filters, grouped summaries, and quick status slices on the Tower page
scope_v1: Read-only filters and summary cards
notes: Keep first tower release minimal before adding richer controls

title: Tower progress planning page
user_value: show the remaining Tower grind in one planning-oriented view instead of piecing it together from summary and detail pages
proposed_solution: add a larger Tower progress page with counts of items left to GM/MM, total mastery remaining, a visual list of remaining items with progress bars, and difficulty breakdown summaries
scope_v1: planning-oriented Tower page with counts of items left to Grand Mastery and Mega Mastery, total mastery remaining, visual remaining-item lists with progress bars, and difficulty breakdown summaries that show both item counts/percent remaining and mastery remaining/percent of target mastery remaining by difficulty; keep this separate from the lightweight Tower summary/filter work
notes: Shipped as a separate Tower Progress route that aggregates by unique item using the highest required tower target per item. The existing Tower page remains the row-by-row status view, while missing mastery difficulty matches stay visible as Unrated and missing snapshot matches are treated as 0 mastery. BL-034 remains the follow-up for accordion drilldown inside difficulty buckets.
release_notes: Added a Tower Progress page with unique-item planning summaries, difficulty breakdowns, and progress bars.

title: Tower progress difficulty drilldown accordion
user_value: make Tower difficulty summaries actionable by letting users open a bucket and inspect the exact outstanding items driving it
proposed_solution: add accordion-style expansion for Tower progress difficulty rows so each difficulty bucket can reveal its outstanding tower items with item-level detail
scope_v1: expandable difficulty breakdown rows on the Tower progress page that show the outstanding tower items in that bucket with item-level detail while preserving independent tower requirement rows and planning-oriented scanability
notes: Keep this as a child of the larger Tower progress planning page rather than folding it into lightweight Tower filters. The expansion grouping should follow the progress page's difficulty buckets and continue treating tower requirement rows as independent even when the same item appears across levels.

title: Snapshot comparison view

scope_v1: Compare two local snapshots without backend

notes: prefer a high-contrast inline alert card over a popup/modal; keep the warning non-fatal

title: Make import placeholder reflect real raw export format

release_notes: Updated the import example to look like a real FarmRPG export and clarified that extra lines are okay.

title: Mastery export instructions page + import help link
user_value: Help users correctly export mastery data from FarmRPG and avoid incomplete imports caused by collapsed accordion sections.
proposed_solution: Create a simple help page with screenshots and step-by-step instructions showing how to export mastery data correctly. Add a "How do I export mastery data?" link on the import screen that opens this help page.

Select and copy the mastery list 4. Paste into the import box; Include example screenshots: Correct export (all tiers expanded) and Incorrect export (collapsed tiers); Add contextual link on the import screen: "How do I export mastery data?"; Link opens the help page
notes: Deferred for now. The mastery page uses collapsible tier sections, which can cause incomplete exports if tiers are collapsed. This documentation should reduce user error and complement the collapsed-tier import warning added in v1.5.2.
release_notes: Added a help page and import link explaining how to copy a complete mastery export.
